This petition is filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act, seeking compensation of Rs.1,00,00,000/- from respondents on account of grievous injuries sustained by petitioner in Road Traffic Accident.

2. The brief facts of the petition are; That, on 10-06-2019 at about 5.45 p.m., petitioner was working at Toyota Kirloskar Company at Bidadi, alighted company mini bus, bearing No.KA-42-A-8354 and the said bus left the company to drop the employees, at about 6.30 p.m., when the said bus reached near Magadi Madavara Nice Road, near Gangondanahalli Bridge, Bengaluru City, the offending vehicle which was driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, who was coming from opposite direction crossed gutter which divides the double road and dashed against mini bus at its back wheel towards the right side, due to the impact mini bus toppled and fell into the gutter.
Due to the impact, petitioner along with other employees sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident petitioner was shifted 3 (SCCH-16) MVC 1081/2020 to Sparsh Super Speciality Hospital,
Yeshwanthpur, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient.

Earlier to the accident, he was working as Engineer in Process Engineering Department, Production Engineering and Services in Toyota Kirloskar Motor Pvt. Ltd., and earning a sum of Rs.63,045/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries he became permanently disabled and whereby lost his earning capacity.
Therefore, petitioner prayed for compensation.

3. Respondent No.2 remained absent and therefore, he was placed exparte.
3(a).

Respondent No.1 admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of Eicher Goods Vehicle,
bearing No.KA-40-A-4127 and its validity as on the date of accident, denied the petition averments generally and contended that respondent No.2 failed to comply the provision under Section 134(C)
and 158(6) of MV Act, the driver of the Eicher Goods Vehicle was not having valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident, vehicle was not having valid permit and fitness certificate to ply in the public place, there is no negligence on the part of the driver of Eicher Goods Vehicle, the driver of the said vehicle drove the same in very slow manner with following all traffic rules and regulations, at that time the driver of bus, bearing No.KA-42-A-8254 drove the same in rash and negligent 4 (SCCH-16) MVC 1081/2020 manner and dashed against Eicher Goods Vehicle, the petition is bad for non joinder of necessary parties as the owner and insurer of bus, bearing No.KA-42-A-8254 are also necessary parties to the proceedings.
Further, it sought for permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.2 under Section 170 of the M.V. Act.
For the above denials and contentions it prayed for dismissal of the petition.

sentences.text:
Discharge summary,
which is at Ex.P12 shows that the petitioner had taken treatment as an inpatient for a period of 3 days in Sparsh Super Speciality Hospital and underwent surgery.
It is averred that because of the injuries he suffered the disablement and from which he lost or lessen his earning capacity.

In proof of the disablement he examined PW2 - Orthopaedic Surgeon from Sparsh Hospital, who assessed the disability of petitioner,
opined that the petitioner suffered physical disability of right arm at 39% and to the whole body at 13%.
His evidences clear that he is not the treated doctor.
No implants implanted.
The fractures came to be united.

Under the facts and circumstances of the case and having regard to the nature of injuries and the fractures came to be united, the disability to the whole body is taken to be considered at its entirety i.e., at 13% as disablement as opined by the doctor.

As per the petitioner's version, prior to the accident, he was working as Engineer in Process Engineering Department, Production Engineering and Services in Toyota Kirloskar Motor Pvt. Ltd.,
and earning a sum of Rs.63,045/- per month.
In substantiation of the same no documents are produced.

The petitioner admitted during his cross- examination that he is working in the same company as he was working earlier to the accident, now he is 10 (SCCH-16) MVC 1081/2020 getting salary of Rs.70,000/- per month, in the month of accident and further months he received the salary.

Hence,
it is clear that he continued his service and the disability didn't came in his way.

As he continued his service as earlier he was doing, it does mean that the petitioner did not lose earning capacity and hence the petitioner is not entitle for loss of future income due to the disability.

Such being the case,
under the facts and circumstances, the question of loss of future income due to permanent disability does not arise.
So, no compensation is considered to be awarded in this particular head.

However, as per the evidence of doctor, the disability suffered by petitioner cannot be ruled out,
which could be considered as physical disablement, it is therefore, it is just and proper to award compensation globally, thus Rs.1,00,000/- under the head physical disablement, on humanitarian ground, is awarded to the petitioner.
Age As per wound the certificate, age of petitioner was 23 years at the time of incident.
It is considered.
Pain and sufferings :

Petitioner sustained severe head injury - left anterior frontal lobe hemorrhagic,
multiple right rib fracture 1st to 10th and left rib fracture 2nd to 5th with left hemopneumothorax and grade IV liver injury with 11 (SCCH-16) MVC 1081/2020 hemoperitoneum.
He underwent surgery.
He suffered pains and sufferings.

It is therefore, it is just and proper to award compensation considering his pains and Sri Kuval J.C vs Bajaj Allianz General Insurance on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195533849/

Laid up period :
The petitioner admitted during his cross- examination that in the month of accident and further months he received the salary.
Hence, it is clear that after the accident he was not applied for any leaves nor sustained any loss of income during the laid up period.
Hence, petitioner is not entitled for compensation under this head.
Medical Bills:

It is averred that the petitioner underwent right arthroscopic bankarts repair surgery on 07-07-2020 and spent a sum of Rs.2,23,863/-, out of which Rs.1,84,160/- was paid by Iffco Tokio General Insurance Co. Ltd., and balance amount of Rs.42,535/-

Amenities and happiness:
It is established that the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
The assessment of disability by the doctor and its consideration as discussed above are to be considered herein.
From such injuries he suffered pains, difficulties, which deprived him of enjoying amenities.
It is therefore, the petitioner is entitle for compensation for loss of his such amenities and happiness.
So, It is deemed proper to award compensation of Rs.75,000/- under this head.
Food, Nourishment, Attendant charges and Conveyance:

Under the facts and circumstances of case having considered the nature of injuries and permanent disablement, though there is no document particularly, it could be presumed that the petitioner might have spent considerable amount for her nutritional food, nourishment, attendant charges and conveyance.
It is therefore, it is opined that for such food, nourishment, attendant charges and for conveyance is concerned awarding of Rs.50,000/- as compensation is just and proper.
Hence, it is considered so.

17 . Insurance policy and its validity are admitted and no breaches are established by the insurer.
As found on the discussions on issue No.1, the negligence was on the part of the driver of the offended Canter Vehicle.
On vicarious liability respondent No.2 being the owner is responsible, respondent No.1 being the insurer of respondent No.2 contractually liable to pay compensation.
Thus, respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
However, initially respondent No.1 is liable to pay the determined compensation.
The petitioner is only entitled to such compensation and not fully as claimed for.
